Westermann (“Between Slavery and Freedom,” American Historical Review , Vol. L [1945]) holds that the “statement of Aristotle . . . that craftsmen live in a condition of limited slavery meant that the artisan, when he made a work contract, disposed of two of the four elements of his free status [viz., of freedom of economic activity and right of unrestricted movement], but by his own volition and for a temporary period”",
